claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy has an enhanced strength–ductility balance.
Removing Co from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alters local lattice distortion.
Removing Co modifies the effective stacking-fault energy.
The changed chemical environment and lattice distortion alter the activation barrier for dislocation glide.
Under suitable temperature and strain-rate conditions, dislocations in Co-free FeNiCrMn periodically lock and unlock through interactions with local solute atmospheres.
The proposed locking and unlocking behavior is analogous to dynamic strain aging.
Periodic dislocation locking and unlocking delays flow or strain localization.
The proposed dislocation mechanism enhances work hardening.
The proposed mechanism sustains ductility while elevating dynamic strength.
The initial Co-free FeNiCrMn material is an as-cast, single-phase solid solution.
The controlled experiment spans room temperature to approximately 600 K and strain rates of approximately 10^-3 to 10^3 s^-1.
Co-free FeNiCrMn and equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi are to be compared under identical tensile-testing conditions.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, Co-free FeNiCrMn should exhibit higher strain-rate sensitivity.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, Co-free FeNiCrMn should exhibit more pronounced serrated flow at intermediate temperatures.
Serrated flow is an indicator of dynamic dislocation locking and unlocking involving solute atmospheres.
The stronger serrated-flow response should correlate with delayed onset of plastic instability.
The Co-free alloy should preserve or improve ductility relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The proposed behavior is expected only from room temperature to approximately 600 K and from approximately 10^-3 to 10^3 s^-1.
Outside the specified regime, low-temperature twinning or high-temperature phase instabilities may dominate deformation.

A lack of statistically significant differences in strain-rate sensitivity and serrated flow, or a lack of corresponding dislocation-locking or solute-atmosphere evidence, would falsify the proposed mechanism.
